papers.title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger: The $\Delta(1232)$ Resonance in Supernova QCD Axion Emission
papers.abstract: The high-energy tail of supernova axion emission controls searches whose response grows with axion energy. We identify a novel production channel, in which the axion is emitted through an intermediate $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which adds a hard component to the spectrum. We calculate the axion production rate from nucleon-nucleon Bremsstrahlung in chiral effective field theory through next-to-leading order. Including the $\Delta(1232)$ roughly doubles the luminosity at one second after bounce and increases the number of escaping axions above $200$ MeV by a factor of about $3$ over the first nine seconds, relative to the nucleon-only calculation. Adding this new production channel roughly doubles $\gamma$-ray counts from conversion in the progenitor's magnetic field and increases water-Cherenkov counts by about an order of magnitude through its combined effects on emission and absorption. The same hard component can mimic a higher core temperature or thermal-pion emission in $\gamma$-ray spectral fits. The $\Delta(1232)$ resonance is therefore crucial for predicting supernova axion signals and interpreting their spectra.
papers.reason: Calculates supernova QCD axion emission including the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance in nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung using chiral EFT, significantly modifying high-energy tails and detection rates.

summary.tldr: Including intermediate $\Delta(1232)$ resonances in nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung substantially hardens the supernova axion spectrum, doubling emission luminosity and increasing water-Cherenkov detection yields by an order of magnitude.
summary.novel_idea: Identifies an omitted production channel in supernova axion emission where $NN \to NNa$ bremsstrahlung proceeds via an intermediate dynamical $\Delta(1232)$ resonance. Because the $\Delta$ is close to its mass shell when $E_a \sim M_\Delta - M_N \approx 293\text{ MeV}$, the narrow resonant propagator overcomes the Boltzmann phase-space suppression, producing a hard high-energy spectral bump that does not rely on a disputed abundance of thermal pions.
summary.method: Formulates the bremsstrahlung amplitude in heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory with dynamical $\Delta$ fields through NLO in the small-scale expansion. Incorporates density-dependent baryon self-energies and in-medium $\Delta$ collisional broadening (using GiBUU inputs) across spherical Garching supernova models (18.6, 18.8, and 20.0 $M_\odot$ with SFHo EoS). Convolutes the resulting rates with magnetic conversion for Fermi-LAT $\gamma$-ray detection and $ap \to p\pi^0$ absorption cross sections for Hyper-Kamiokande.
key_results: For a hot $20.0\,M_\odot$ core, the $\Delta$ channel overtakes nucleon-only bremsstrahlung above $E_a \approx 175\text{ MeV}$ and increases the spectral intensity at $E_a = 293\text{ MeV}$ by a factor of 2.3.
Total axion luminosity roughly doubles at 1 s post-bounce, while escaping axion counts above $200\text{ MeV}$ over the first 9 s increase by a factor of $\sim 3$.

Water-Cherenkov event yields in Hyper-Kamiokande via $ap \to p\pi^0$ increase by a factor of $9.1^{+2.7}_{-5.0}$ due to the compound enhancement of harder emission and $\Delta$-mediated detector absorption.

Omitting the $\Delta$ resonance in $\gamma$-ray spectral templates biases reconstructed supernova core temperatures upward by $9\text{--}22\text{ MeV}$ and can falsely mimic thermal pion conversion at the $5\text{--}22\%$ level.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to your work on chiral EFT electroweak and light-mediator interactions, in-medium resonance dynamics (interfacing with transport tools like GiBUU), and low-energy supernova detection signals in large underground detectors.
summary.caveats: Calculations evaluate the strong interaction in one-pion exchange Born approximation without iterating the nucleon-nucleon tensor force or including $NNN\Delta$ contact terms; external $\Delta$ states in the equation of state are also neglected.

papers.title: QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay at order $\alpha^2$
papers.abstract: We compute two-loop QED corrections to neutron and nuclear beta decay, including full electron mass dependence and real radiation contributions. The result for the neutron, $\delta_{R,\,\rm static}= ( 29.199 \pm 0.001 )\times 10^{-3}$, implies a factor $\sim 70 $ reduction in the uncertainty of the low-energy radiative corrections compared to previous results obtained in the large energy/small electron-mass limit, $m_e/(m_n-m_p) \to 0$. For superallowed nuclear decays we find that the $Z$-independent order $\alpha^2$ corrections range from $(0.1-0.5) \times 10^{-4}$ i.e., of roughly the expected size and comparable to current uncertainty estimates.
papers.topic: Two-loop QED corrections to beta decay
papers.reason: Computes exact two-loop QED corrections for neutron and nuclear beta decay with full electron mass dependence, directly in the reader's core precision electroweak interest. [favorite author: Richard Hill]

summary.tldr: Complete two-loop $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay are calculated with exact electron mass dependence, reducing low-energy radiative correction uncertainties to the $10^{-6}$ level.
summary.novel_idea: Provides the first complete calculation of two-loop $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ virtual, real-virtual, and double-real QED corrections to neutron and superallowed nuclear $\beta$-decay retaining full electron mass ($m_e/E$) dependence. This eliminates the dominant theoretical systematic in the low-energy radiative correction $\delta_{R,\text{static}}$, reducing its uncertainty by a factor of $\sim 70$.
summary.method: Computes two-loop form factors within heavy-particle electron effective theory using both direct timelike diagram evaluation and a subtracted dispersion relation over background-field cuts. Integrates the 18 master integrals by transforming differential equations to canonical $\epsilon$-form with Goncharov polylogarithms, fixing boundary conditions at zero recoil $w=1$. Combines virtual amplitudes with real-virtual, double-real, and pair-production phase space using a soft-photon slicing prescription.
key_results: Determines the static neutron radiative correction to be $\delta_{R,\text{static}} = (29.199 \pm 0.001) \times 10^{-3}$, reducing previous theory error from $\pm 0.07 \times 10^{-3}$ to $\pm 0.001 \times 10^{-3}$.
Performs the first direct QED computation of the two-loop zero-recoil heavy-light matching coefficient $E(m)$, analytically confirming the Czarnecki-Melnikov-Grozin result.

Computes phase-space-averaged $Z$-independent $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ corrections $\langle \delta^{(2,0)} \rangle$ for 15 superallowed $0^+ \to 0^+$ emitters, showing they contribute $(0.1\text{--}0.5) \times 10^{-4}$ to $\delta_R'$, matching experimental precision in $|V_{ud}|$.
Confirms full agreement with recent independent calculations (Crosas and Mereghetti) regarding electron-mass dependence in the $Z\alpha^2$ nuclear corrections.
summary.why_it_matters: A must-read by favorite authors Richard Hill and Ryan Plestid. It definitively nails the long-distance QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay, ensuring that low-energy QED systematics are now negligible in $|V_{ud}|$ and CKM unitarity extractions.
summary.caveats: The calculation operates in the static nucleon limit; nuclear-structure dependent corrections ($\delta_{\text{NS}}$) and hadronic axial-vector inner radiative corrections (the box diagrams) remain external and dominate the overall $|V_{ud}|$ uncertainty.

papers.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
papers.abstract: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results. These examples also show its ability to search the literature, analyze non-power-law spectra using user-provided model code, and develop new analysis functions, such as signal-injection simulations. \system is also a powerful tool for improving and testing existing analysis code, as we demonstrate by using it to refine the background probability density functions and reduce residuals and spurious signal contributions in stacking analyses. \system makes high-energy neutrino data analysis more accessible to the broader research community. Code and usage instructions: \href{https://github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}{\faGithub\ {\tt github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}}.
papers.reason: Presents a public AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches using IceCube data, perfectly aligning with ML/AI agent workflows for neutrino phenomenology.

summary.tldr: NuSrcAgent is an LLM-powered AI agent that automates IceCube high-energy neutrino source searches and catalog stacking through natural-language conversation while preserving full analysis reproducibility.
summary.novel_idea: Builds the first dedicated conversational AI agent for high-energy neutrino astronomy. It wraps unbinned likelihood analysis tools on public IceCube data (IceTracks-DR2), generates verifiable structured commands, enforces strict input checks, and writes custom code on-the-fly for user-specified non-power-law models and signal injections.
summary.method: Connects LLMs (Codex or Claude Code) via a specialized instructions module to an underlying analysis engine (`run_agent_wrap.py`). Implements an unbinned time-integrated and time-dependent likelihood framework supporting single sources, catalog scans, and stacking. Integrates an improved 'v3' background PDF algorithm utilizing adaptive sliding windows to mitigate energy proxy binning residuals.
key_results: Accurately reproduces IceCube's 14-year IceTracks-DR2 analysis of NGC 1068, matching public SkyLLH best-fit parameters ($\hat{n} \approx 98$, $\text{TS} \approx 22.8$).
Demonstrates automated code generation and execution for non-power-law neutrino spectra from turbulent accretion disk corona models directly from user-supplied GitHub repositories.
The newly introduced v3 background PDFs eliminate unphysical energy residuals at $0.6\text{--}1\text{ TeV}$, preventing spurious signal counts that previously biased stacking analyses.
Validates autonomous catalog scans and stacking on 387 dust-echo-like infrared flares and magnetar catalogs, matching published trial distributions.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a useful case study in designing reliable, verifiable LLM agent workflows for phenomenological neutrino analysis, demonstrating how to prevent LLM hallucinations via wrapper validations and reproducible run records.
summary.caveats: Limited to public IceCube muon-track data releases; the accuracy of novel ad-hoc code written by the agent depends on the user's scrutiny of the generated scripts and background PDFs.

papers.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
papers.abstract: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $\nu_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.
papers.topic: Flavor composition of Milky Way neutrinos
papers.reason: Evaluates how IceCube and KM3NeT can measure the flavor composition of Galactic high-energy neutrinos to test sources and neutrino decay, directly hitting core high-energy neutrino phenomenology.

summary.tldr: Future multi-observatory neutrino telescope networks can measure the Milky Way's neutrino flavor composition to within 27%, distinguishing production mechanisms and probing neutrino decay up to $\tau/m \sim 1.5 \times 10^4\text{ s/eV}$.
summary.novel_idea: Proposes using the measured flavor composition of the Galactic plane as an unoscillated, decay-free astrophysical baseline. Comparing this Galactic reference against the diffuse extragalactic neutrino flux breaks degeneracies between source magnetic field cooling (muon damping) and BSM neutrino decay over cosmological distances.
summary.method: Performs an Asimov binned-Poisson $\chi^2$ sensitivity forecast incorporating 8 running, under-construction, and proposed neutrino observatories (IceCube, KM3NeT, Baikal-GVD, P-ONE, TRIDENT, NEON, HUNT, IceCube-Gen2). Tracks, showers, and double cascades are modeled across three Galactic longitude segments and the diffuse extragalactic sky, profiling over 55 systematic nuisance parameters.
key_results: IceCube (15 yr) combined with KM3NeT (10 yr) can reject pure neutron-decay production ($f_{e,\text{S}}=1$, pure $\bar{\nu}_e$) in the inner Galaxy at $\sim 2\sigma$.

The full eight-telescope network will determine the source electron fraction $f_{e,\text{S}}$ in the inner Galaxy to within 27% at 68% C.L., separating standard pion decay ($f_{e,\text{S}}=1/3$) from muon damping ($f_{e,\text{S}}=0$) at $3\sigma$.

Comparing Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions extends sensitivity to neutrino mass eigenstate decay ($
u_2, 
u_3 	o 
u_1$) up to $	au/m \approx 1.5 	imes 10^4	ext{ s/eV}$, improving upon current extragalactic bounds by a factor of 70.
Extragalactic muon synchrotron cooling can be detected at $3\sigma$ ($5\sigma$) for source classes with mean magnetic fields $B \gtrsim 11\text{ kG}$ ($22\text{ kG}$).
summary.why_it_matters: Offers an interesting perspective on using high-energy neutrino flavor ratios as a probe of BSM neutrino properties (specifically neutrino invisible decay), complementing laboratory neutrino oscillation programs.
summary.caveats: Relies on idealized response projections for six future facilities that are not yet constructed; assumes that flavor ratios are energy-independent across the TeV--PeV range.

papers.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
papers.abstract: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,\mu,\tau$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_\mu-L_\tau$ force from neutron star binaries.
papers.topic: Screening of new Abelian long-range forces
papers.reason: Investigates how Higgs mechanism screening modifies astrophysical and laboratory bounds on U(1) forces and neutrino oscillations, squarely fitting the BSM/long-range force interest.

summary.tldr: When ultralight gauge bosons acquire mass via the Higgs mechanism, scalar screening displaces the field in large celestial bodies, substantially weakening fifth-force and neutrino-oscillation bounds on $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$ forces.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrates that UV-completing an ultralight gauge mediator into the Abelian Higgs Model (AHM) introduces vector charge screening around astronomical bodies. Large macroscopic charges drive the scalar field away from its vacuum expectation value, generating effective in-medium masses that screen the gauge field and invalidate naive Proca-theory exclusion limits.
summary.method: Solves the coupled classical nonlinear equations of motion for the gauge potential $A^0$ and scalar field $|\phi|$ for spherically symmetric, static charge distributions (Earth, Sun, neutron stars). Classifies screening into thin-shell ($m_{\phi,\text{eff}}R \gg 1$) and gradient ($m_{\phi,\text{eff}}R \ll 1$) regimes governed by $\tilde{g} = g/\sqrt{\lambda} = m_V/(\sqrt{2}m_\phi)$, mapping the modified field profiles onto experimental bounds.
key_results: For gauged $B-L$, screening reduces the interaction range; for $\tilde{g} \gtrsim 10$, MICROSCOPE satellite limits vanish for $g \gtrsim 10^{-24}$, opening an unconstrained parameter window $10^{-24} \lesssim g \lesssim 10^{-23}$ before Eöt-Wash constraints apply.

For $L_e - L_{\mu/\tau}$ symmetries, solar screening suppresses the flavor-electric potential at Earth's orbit for $\tilde{g} \gtrsim 10^{-4}$, evading solar-induced matter effects in terrestrial neutrino oscillation experiments.

Solar neutrino oscillation limits on $L_e - L_{\mu/\tau}$ relax as $g \propto \tilde{g}$, rendering terrestrial baseline oscillation searches more constraining than solar neutrino bounds for $\tilde{g} \gtrsim 10^{-3}$.
For $L_\mu - L_\tau$, strong screening inside neutron stars eliminates dipole radiation in neutron star binaries, evading orbital period decay constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: Crucial for interpreting matter-induced neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) and ultralight mediator bounds in neutrino oscillation experiments (DUNE, solar/atmospheric neutrinos), proving that bounds from long-range forces are strongly model-dependent when the vector mass is dynamical.
summary.caveats: Screening from localized surrounding topography for terrestrial torsion balances at $m_V > 10^{-13}\text{ eV}$ was not comprehensively simulated; binary neutron star screening was evaluated in a quasi-static regime.

papers.title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
papers.abstract: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor evolution of dense neutrino gases interacting with their surroundings, particularly in explosive astrophysical environments.
papers.reason: Investigates collisional neutrino-flavor instabilities in dense neutrino gases, detailing energy, angular, and inhomogeneity structures.

summary.tldr: A linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations reveal that anisotropic neutrino backgrounds alter the wavenumber dependence of collisional flavor instabilities, producing distinct near/gapless and far/gapped branches.
summary.novel_idea: The work extends previous studies on collisional flavor conversion (CFC) in isotropic and homogeneous neutrino gases to multi-energy, multi-angle, and spatially inhomogeneous systems with anisotropic distributions.
summary.method: The author performs a linear stability analysis using the dispersion relation of quantum kinetic equations and conducts direct nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations to track the resulting flavor evolution, spatial mode coupling, and decoherence.
key_results: Near/gapless modes exhibit maximum growth rates localized near the zero mode, whereas far/gapped modes peak at finite collective-scale wavenumbers.

Eigenvectors of near/gapless modes show strong energy dependence ($	imes 1/(1+E_
u^2)$), while far/gapped modes are energy-insensitive and forward-peaked.
Collisional decoherence limits the growth of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous despite mode-coupling cascades.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to neutrino event generators and quantum kinetic treatments of dense neutrino transport in core-collapse supernovae and neutron-star mergers, where interaction modelling and collective phenomena intersect.
summary.caveats: The analysis assumes specific relaxation-form collision terms and ignores heavy-leptonic opacities ($	au_x = 0$) and classical relaxation processes.

papers.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
papers.abstract: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.
papers.reason: Derives a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass using resonant self-interactions of ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the cosmic neutrino background.

summary.tldr: Resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the cosmic neutrino background via an MeV-scale mediator places a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass when confronted with IceCube HESE data.
summary.novel_idea: Utilizing the transition and ultra-relativistic regimes of $s$-channel resonant scattering between cosmic relic neutrinos and UHE neutrinos—incorporating double transport equations and double regeneration terms—to constrain the absolute mass scale from below.
summary.method: Derivation from first principles of double transport equations with double regeneration terms for coupled neutrino and antineutrino evolution, followed by a likelihood analysis comparing simulated event spectra against 7.5 years of IceCube HESE data.
key_results: The best-fit parameters are found at $m_{	ext{lightest}} = 7.4 	imes 10^{-3}$ eV (NO) and $1.1 	imes 10^{-2}$ eV (IO) with a mediator mass $m_	heta  acksimeq 2.6$ MeV.
For $m_	heta = 1$ MeV and $g_{	au	au} = 0.01$, a lower bound is established: $m_{	ext{lightest}} > 7.76 	imes 10^{-3}$ eV (NO) and $7.82 	imes 10^{-3}$ eV (IO) at 95% C.L.
Combining the HESE lower bound with DESI cosmological upper bounds restricts the lightest neutrino mass to a narrow window around $10^{-2}$ eV.
summary.why_it_matters: Connects ultra-high-energy neutrino astronomy, BSM neutrino self-interactions (LEFT/SMEFT contexts), and absolute neutrino mass measurements from cosmology and scattering.
summary.caveats: The results depend on assumed source flavor compositions, power-law spectra, and specific choices of the $	au$-flavored neutrino self-interaction coupling constant.

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.
papers.reason: Addresses temperature-parameter inference and local identifiability in neutrino oscillation dephasing models with MSW energy diversity.

summary.tldr: Energy-resolved sampling in MSW-driven neutrino propagation can resolve identifiability degeneracies in multiparameter open-system thermometry, though the absolute thermal fluctuation imprint in the Sun remains extremely small.
summary.novel_idea: Formulates solar-neutrino propagation as a quantum metrology and thermometry problem, proving that energy diversity lifts the rank-one degeneracy of the quantum Fisher information matrix in a two-zone temperature model.
summary.method: Uses an open-system quantum master equation approach, evaluating the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM), symmetric logarithmic derivatives, and local Debye-cell plasma noise benchmarks for neutrino oscillations.
key_results: In a single-energy longitudinal dephasing limit, a two-zone temperature model yields a QFIM of rank at most 1, making separate temperature inference impossible.
Independent energy-resolved samples with noncollinear thermal-sensitivity vectors restore full rank.
A heuristic electron-only Debye-cell estimate yields a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of $∳ 3.1 	imes 10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV over one solar radius.
summary.why_it_matters: Brings rigorous quantum estimation theory, quantum entanglement, and noise benchmarking tools into contact with low-energy solar neutrino oscillations and matter effects.
summary.caveats: Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping, and the Debye-cell model is a heuristic order-of-magnitude estimate rather than a full plasma-response calculation.

papers.title: Majorana Neutrino Exchange in Free-Baryon $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ Reactions
papers.abstract: The free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to pp e^-e^-$ are studied for six nonstrange and strange initial states, with light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange treated in the same baryon-level framework. For light-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with the square of the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. The calculated cross sections increase as the off-shell cutoff $\Delta q^2$ is reduced, especially near threshold and in the hyperon channels, because more of the phase-space region where the squared four-momentum of the exchanged neutrino is close to zero is retained. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28\times10^{-49}$--$1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{\beta\beta}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. For heavy-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with $\eta_N^2$, where $\eta_N=|U_{eN}|^2/m_N$. The leading propagator correction remains below one percent for $m_N\gtrsim50~\mathrm{GeV}$ over the phase-space region considered. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$--$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $\eta_N=4.0\times10^{-9}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. At higher energies, the two exchange cases give the same CKM-driven channel ordering, with the $nn$ cross section largest. At fixed $\sqrt{s}$, compared with the light-neutrino spectra calculated with $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mbox{GeV}^2$, the heavy-neutrino peaks occur at a smaller squared invariant mass for the proton pair and a larger one for the electron pair. These results extend the free-baryon analogue of neutrinoless double-beta decay to strange initial states and provide theoretical reference results for comparing light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange.
papers.reason: Studies free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ for light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange within a unified baryon-level framework.

summary.tldr: Free-baryon reactions $B_1 B_2 	o p p e^- e^-$ are evaluated for six nonstrange and strange initial states within a unified baryon-level framework for light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange.
summary.novel_idea:

summary.method: Constructs antisymmetrized amplitudes using momentum-dependent dipole weak form factors (vector and axial-vector currents), exact four-body phase space, and an off-shell cutoff $Δ q^2$ for the exchanged light neutrino.
key_results: Light-neutrino cross sections scale as $m_{ eta eta}^2$ and increase as $Δ q^2$ decreases due to retention of phase space near $q^2 = 0$.
At $\sqrt{s} = 5.1$ GeV, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28 	imes 10^{-49}$ to $1.78 	imes 10^{-45}$ $	ext{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{ eta eta} = 30$ meV and $Δ q^2 = 10^{-2}$ $	ext{GeV}^2$.
Heavy-neutrino cross sections scale with $ͷ_N^2 = (|U_{eN}|^2 / m_N)^2$, with propagator corrections below 1% for $m_N ≳ 50$ GeV.
At fixed $\sqrt{s}$, heavy-neutrino spectra peak at smaller squared invariant mass for the proton pair ($m_{pp}^2$) and larger for the electron pair ($m_{ee}^2$) compared to light-neutrino exchange.
summary.why_it_matters:
Directly connects to nuclear/baryonic matrix elements for $0

summary.caveats: Short-range two-nucleon/baryon interactions, Coulomb forces, and hadronic currents beyond leading vector and axial-vector terms (such as weak-magnetism and induced pseudoscalar form factors) are omitted.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Dark Matter at the Electroweak Scale
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter provides an explanation for astrophysical evidence for dark matter at all scales. This non-thermal dark matter requires a misalignment mechanism to reproduce the observed matter energy density of the Universe and therefore induce oscillating, time-dependent signals. We determine the sensitivity of current and future collider measurements of the width of the Z and Higgs bosons, and show that CP odd observables such as dipole moments in $Z\to \tau^+\tau^-$ decays provide a better sensitivity to ultralight dark matter than atomic clocks or equivalence principle tests.
papers.topic: Ultralight dark matter at EW scale
papers.reason: Examines colliders, Z/Higgs widths, and CP-odd observables to probe ultralight dark matter, aligning with precision probes of new physics.

summary.tldr: CP-odd observables such as tau-lepton dipole moments in $Z 	o 	au^+	au^-$ decays provide superior sensitivity to ultralight dark matter (ULDM) compared to atomic clocks, equivalence principle tests, or CP-even collider width measurements.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrating that while CP-even collider observables (like $Z$ and Higgs widths) and precision low-energy sensors suffer from quadratic suppression in fine-constant variations, CP-odd dipole operators scale linearly, making them uniquely competitive probes of ULDM.
summary.method: Analyses of LEP $Z$-resonance line-shape fits, future FCC-ee $Z$ and Higgs width projections, and time-resolved versus time-integrated quad-fitting of CP-odd spin correlations in $Z 	o 	au^+	au^-$ decays.
key_results: LEP data and FCC-ee projections constrain CP-even interactions (e.g., $Z$ mass/width oscillations), but are superseded by atomic clock and MICROSCOPE equivalence-principle limits.
Time-resolved analyses of $Z 	o 	au^+	au^-$ dipoles at FCC-ee overcome time-integrated cancellation nodes when $N_{	ext{osc}} ≳ 1$.
For ULDM masses $m_	heta = 10^{-24}$--$10^{-18}$ eV, projected FCC-ee dipole measurements achieve better sensitivity than current atomic clock comparisons.
summary.why_it_matters: Brings precision electroweak collider physics (LEP, FCC-ee) into the realm of ultralight dark matter detection, matching and exceeding precision atomic probes via novel CP-odd observables.
summary.caveats: Relies on effective field theory operator matching and assumes specific two-loop electroweak matching coefficients are order-one by dimensional analysis.

papers.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
papers.abstract: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $K_L\to\pi^0\nu\bar\nu$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.
papers.topic: CKM CP violation in EDMs and rare decays
papers.reason: Connects paramagnetic EDMs, rare kaon decays, and CKM matrix elements without relying on B-decay inputs, fitting precision flavor physics with a low-energy angle.

papers.title: Rational terms and UV counterterms of the SMEFT at next-to-leading order in QCD
papers.abstract: We compute the rational terms $R_2$ and the ultraviolet counterterms of the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD without any flavour assumption, for complex Wilson coefficients, massive quarks and a general CKM matrix. We also compute the on-shell renormalisation factors of the quark fields in the presence of flavour mixing. We work with an anticommuting $\gamma_5$ and read closed fermion loops with a single $\gamma_5$ at the operator insertion. The results, also for common flavour assumptions, are provided in electronic form and in a Mathematica package attached to the paper. We use them to build example models for MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and give NLO predictions for representative processes.
papers.topic: SMEFT NLO QCD and rational terms
papers.reason: Provides NLO QCD calculations for SMEFT with massive quarks and CKM mixing, directly useful for EFT matching and neutrino/flavor observables.

papers.title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
papers.abstract: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{a\gamma}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{a\gamma}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.
papers.reason: Proposes a stratospheric balloon optical link to search for ultralight axion dark matter via photon coupling, aligning with precision probes of new physics.

papers.title: Direct mass measurements of the high-spin isomers in self-conjugate 94Ag
papers.abstract: Two decades ago, two-proton emission from a $(21^+)$ isomeric state in $^{94}$Ag was reported. This report has remained the sole example of possible two-proton radioactivity in a nucleus with an odd number of protons on the chart of nuclei. A debate regarding the viability of the decay mode has been ongoing due to the unknown mass of the isomer. Here, using state-selective laser ionization in a hot cavity catcher, we present multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometry of the long-lived isomeric states of $^{94}$Ag and its one-proton decay daughter $^{93}$Pd. For the first time, direct mass measurements of the $(7^+)$ and $(21^+)$ isomeric states set the stage for an independent discussion of the energetics of these decays. We rule out the two-proton emission from the $(21^+)$ state as previously reported and reveal the one-proton decay energy to be significantly lower. State-of-the-art shell-model calculations reproduce the energy gap of the $(7^+)$ and the $(21^+)$ states as well as the half-life of the $(21^+)$ state, implying the $(21^+)$ state is likely near-spherical, contradicting the reported explanation for the two-proton radioactivity. Importantly, the techniques employed are a stepping stone towards the first laser spectroscopic investigation of a proton-emitting state
papers.reason: Provides direct mass measurements and shell-model calculations of high-spin isomers in proton-rich nuclei, highly relevant to nuclear structure inputs for electroweak decays.

papers.title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
papers.abstract: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.
papers.reason: Analyzes twist-3 quark-gluon correlations and the pion's chiral-odd distribution amplitude within Dyson-Schwinger equations, specifically restoring Wilson line EOM sum rules.

papers.title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
papers.abstract: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.
papers.reason: Explores a leptophilic t-channel dark sector explaining the LZ high-recoil event via inelastic endothermic scattering.

papers.title: Tackling the DVCS inverse problem with finite element method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we tackle the problem of shadow GPDs, arising from the non-invertibility of the measured $2\to 2$ exclusive processes at large virtualities (DVCS, TCS and DVMP). This problem arose five years ago as the main source of theoretical uncertainties, potentially dominating experimental ones by orders of magnitude. We show here that the deconvolution ambiguity can be elegantly eliminated by relying on finite element method. The problem is essentially converted at any finite discretisation area $a$ from a non-invertible to an ill-conditioned one. Given experimental uncertainties, this yields a theoretical lower bound on the discretisation area $a_\textrm{min}$, that can be interpreted as the maximal theoretical resolution one can obtain on the reconstruction of the lightcone momentum fractions. Associated with the local polynomial degree $p$, the pair $(a,p)$ provides an insightful and easily understandable regularisation framework, allowing one to systematically improve the description of the momentum fractions dependence of GPDs with the pQCD order at which the hard kernels of exclusive processes are computed.
papers.reason: Tackles the deconvolution and inverse problem for exclusive processes like DVCS, highly relevant given the connection between electron scattering and neutrino cross-section constraints.

papers.title: Microscopic Approach to Neutron Elastic and Inelastic Cross Sections
papers.abstract: Depending on the nuclei involved and the beam energies, reaction timescales differ tremendously. Today, distinct models are often used to describe each timescale, relying on phenomenological inputs, such as level densities or partial-widths, which limits their predictive power. This work aims to address this issue by providing a unified description of low-energy neutron elastic and inelastic reaction channels starting from microscopic predictions of the structure of mid-mass nuclei. The goal is to build a framework that is general enough to span the different reaction regimes while remaining anchored in microscopic theory. For illustration purposes, this work focuses on reactions $n+^{20}$Ne to the elastic and inelastic channels. The S-matrix is build from shell model predictions of resonances states and their spectroscopic amplitudes for $^{21}$Ne, using two different approximations of the single-particle asymptotics. Then, the shell-model predictions for the level density and single-particle partial widths are analyzed and the final cross sections are compared with evaluated ones. This method qualitatively reproduces the ENDF evaluation for the $^{20}$Ne$(n,el)$ and $^{20}$Ne$(n,n')$ cross sections. The present study also compares the Shannon entropy obtained from this model to the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE). In the future, the framework will be extended to include more complex reaction channels, such as two-nucleon and gamma channels, enabling more accurate predictions of neutron-induced reactions such as those of astrophysical interest.
papers.reason: Provides a microscopic framework for neutron-nucleus elastic and inelastic scattering using shell-model resonance states, relevant to nuclear inputs for neutrino interactions.

papers.title: Letter of Intent: AN Underground Belayed In-Shaft (ANUBIS) detector
papers.abstract: Long-lived particles (LLPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, notably in models with dark matter candidates or motivated by baryogenesis. LLPs produced at or above the electroweak scale with decay lengths of tens of metres escape the general-purpose LHC detectors and cannot be produced at sufficient rates in forward and beam-dump experiments. This Letter of Intent proposes the ANUBIS detector, which would instrument the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern and the bottom of its access shafts with about 1600~m$^2$ of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers about 1~m apart, using the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector as decay volume. The ANUBIS detector exploits the full ATLAS event information to suppress backgrounds, and exchanges triggers with the ATLAS experiment. With 3~ab$^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC, it would improve the sensitivity to exotic Higgs-boson decays into long-lived scalars by two to three orders of magnitude, probe heavy neutral leptons of all three flavours down to mixings of about $2\times10^{-8}$, and extend the reach for axion-like particles. The \textsl{pro}ANUBIS demonstrator, operated in the ATLAS cavern in 2024 and 2025, has validated the detector technology. The detector design, trigger concept, integration with the ATLAS experiment and a timeline towards installation in LHC Long Shutdown 4 are presented.
papers.reason: Proposes a new LHC-based cavern detector to search for long-lived particles, heavy neutral leptons, and ALPs, matching interests in BSM searches at neutrino/particle facilities.

papers.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
papers.abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.
papers.topic: Gradient-flow scale from octet baryon masses
papers.reason: Uses covariant chiral perturbation theory to determine the gradient-flow scale from lattice QCD baryon masses, relevant to low-energy QCD and nucleon properties.

papers.title: Heavy-flavor transverse energy-energy correlators in the color-glass condensate
papers.abstract: We calculate the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) for forward heavy-quark pair production in proton--nucleus collisions at leading order within the Color Glass Condensate framework. The calculation retains the heavy--quark mass, exact final-state parton kinematics and full relative azimuthal-angle dependence, without imposing a back-to-back approximation. Within the adopted collinear fragmentation prescription, a complete sum over hadron species in the two heavy-quark fragmentation branches eliminates the fragmentation functions through the momentum sum rule. We present numerical results for charm production at RHIC energies and charm and bottom production at LHC energies, using HERA-constrained McLerran--Venugopalan initial conditions evolved with the running-coupling Balitsky--Kovchegov equation. Relative to proton--proton collisions, the nuclear target suppresses the integrated TEEC per nucleon and shifts the relative angular weight towards configurations farther from back-to-back. The magnitude and angular dependence of these modifications vary with the quark mass, collision kinematics and nuclear geometry. These results illustrate the sensitivity of heavy-flavor energy correlations to nuclear small-$x$ dynamics while reducing their leading collinear fragmentation dependence.
papers.reason: Calculates transverse energy-energy correlators for heavy quarks in pA collisions, relevant to QCD resummation and small-x dynamics.

papers.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
papers.abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.
papers.reason: Performs tensor network calculations of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions in a NJL model, relevant for partonic structure approaches.

papers.title: Higgsino dark matter explanation of LZ high-recoil event from deflected AMSB with $U(1)_X$ generated $\mu$ term
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent LZ high-recoil event, we propose to study the Higgsino dark matter in a supersymmetric $U(1)_X$ framework with one charged visible singlet. The gauge symmetry forbids the bare Higgs bilinear and the cubic $S^3$ while allowing the singlet interaction that generates an effective Higgsino mass after symmetry breaking. We present the six-state neutralino mixing matrix, including the $U(1)_X$ gaugino and the singlino, and the resulting neutral Higgsino mass splitting. Different deflected-anomaly-mediated parameter regimes provide the soft-mass hierarchies needed for light, 1.1 TeV and heavy Higgsino candidates. The cosmological consequences of the messenger sector in deflected AMSB can affect greatly the thermal history of the dark matter. Late messenger decays can supplement an underabundant thermal population or dilute an overabundant one through entropy production. These possibilities are governed by a common final-yield relation: a dominating messenger must have sufficiently suppressed Higgsino production for net dilution to succeed. We organise the 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV and 100 TeV reference regimes around this condition. Direct-detection and solar-capture constraints are discussed as tests of the resulting spectrum and final abundance. The elastic bino- or singlino-like interpretation of the same event is also realized in this spectrum: the Higgsino asymmetry $|X_A|\simeq10^{-2}$ that a $248\keV$ recoil requires arises without tuning, with a spin-dependent rate lying close to the present experimental sensitivity.
papers.reason: Proposes a supersymmetric U(1)X Higgsino dark matter scenario to explain the LZ high-recoil event via deflected AMSB.

papers.title: Complete NNLO QCD Calculations of $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ Form Factors and Semileptonic Decays
papers.abstract: We present the first complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD calculation of all 34 vector, axial-vector, tensor, and axial-tensor form factors for the four $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ transitions within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. Using automated multi-loop techniques based on \texttt{FeynCalc} and \texttt{AMFlow}, we provide a dataset with at least 40 significant digits at 35 exact rational points in the $(m_b,m_c,q^2)$ parameter space, covering $q^2\in[-10,10]~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. In the spacelike region ($q^2<0$) and near $q^2=0$, the NLO corrections typically enhance the LO form factors by $\mathcal{O}(70\%)$, while the NNLO corrections amount to $\mathcal{O}(20\%)$ of the NLO predictions and substantially reduce the renormalization-scale dependence, demonstrating good perturbative convergence. In contrast, fixed-order NRQCD predictions suffer from threshold instabilities and become less reliable at higher timelike $q^2$. We therefore extrapolate the form factors to the full physical region via $z$-series fits to the NRQCD results at spacelike and near-zero $q^2$, finding broad agreement with the latest lattice QCD results for $B_c\to J/\psi$. With the resulting NRQCD+$z$-series form factors, we predict the decay widths, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor-universality (LFU) ratios for $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)\,\ell\nu_\ell$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) at LO, NLO, and NNLO. Higher-order corrections substantially enhance the absolute rates but largely cancel in the ratios, whose uncertainties are dominated by the choice of fitting points. In particular, our NNLO central prediction $\mathcal{R}(B_c\to J/\psi)=0.2836$ lies between the latest lattice QCD determination and the most recent LHCb measurement.
papers.topic: NNLO Bc to J/psi form factors
papers.reason: Performs complete NNLO QCD calculations of $B_c^{(*)}	o J/\eta_c$ form factors and semileptonic decays within NRQCD factorization.

papers.title: Large-scale fission properties with BSkG3 I : fission paths and spontaneous fission half-lives
papers.abstract: We present our first large-scale analysis of nuclear fission properties based on the BSkG3 energy density functional. Building on the model's unprecedented agreement with ground state observables and fission data in the actinide region, we survey nearly 3300 nuclei with $80\leq Z\leq118$, spanning the region between the predicted proton and neutron drip lines. We calculate thousands of potential energy surfaces that explicitly account for triaxial and octupole deformations. We determine the corresponding least-action fission paths using microscopic collective inertias derived consistently from BSkG3 and calculate spontaneous fission (SF) half-lives within the semiclassical WKB approximation. Our results reveal a rich diversity of fission path topologies, extending well beyond the conventional two-humped picture commonly adopted in reaction codes, and a wide variety of nuclear shapes along these paths, highlighting the limitations of exploring only one collective degree of freedom. In particular, triaxiality affects not only inner barriers in the actinide region but also outer barriers and single barriers in several regions of the superheavy nuclei. Our predicted SF half-lives follow trends similar to those of previous large-scale studies, although significant differences emerge near the neutron drip line. The resulting dataset, including fission barriers, SF half-lives, and saddle-point nuclear level densities, is available has been incorporated into the TALYS reaction code and the BRUSLIB repository. It provides a microscopic foundation for nuclear reaction calculations and astrophysical applications, particularly rapid neutron-capture simulations, which require reliable fission properties of nuclei far from the valley of stability.
papers.reason: Presents a large-scale analysis of fission paths and spontaneous fission half-lives for thousands of nuclei using the BSkG3 energy density functional.

papers.title: Confronting $b \to (s, d)\mu^+ \mu^-$ and $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ puzzle in a $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ framework with neutrino phenomenology
papers.abstract: Current data on several observables in $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions reveal certain discrepancies with Standard Model (SM) predictions. Considering the possibility that these deviations stem from new physics, we explore a $Z^{\prime}$ framework based on $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ model. The parameter space is examined in light of existing constraints from $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions. Within this framework, we show that the quark couplings accommodating $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ anomalies, imprint correlated signatures on the non-leptonic puzzles $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ in $B_{s(d)} \to K^{{*}}\bar{K}^{{*}}$ decays. We find that the scenario with both vector and axial-vector contributions of opposite sign is favored by the data compared to pure vector contribution, offering a correlated probe of the underlying new-physics scenario. We further explore the neutrino phenomenology within the same framework in light of current data.
papers.reason: Explores B-anomalies and neutrino phenomenology in a U(1) extension, adjacent to BSM neutrino physics.

papers.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.
papers.topic: Look-Elsewhere Effect in new physics searches
papers.reason: Reviews statistical challenges like the LEE in classical and machine-learning searches for new physics, useful for experimental data analysis.

papers.title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
papers.abstract: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.
papers.topic: Time-weighted energy correlators in gauge theories
papers.reason: Analyzes infrared safety of time-weighted energy correlators, relevant to perturbative QCD and parton showers.

papers.title: The String Theory Photinoverse
papers.abstract: Type-IIB string compactifications typically give rise to a significant number of RR-photons. These are generically massless and do not possess any light charged states, making them `superhidden'. However, since supersymmetry is present at least at some high scale, corresponding `dark photinos' are also predicted. The kinetic mixing of the photons together with the SUSY breaking mass terms of the photinos makes the latter observable. We identify geometries in which the mixing is induced by Wilson lines and show that their expectation values are generically non-zero. As a result, most of the dark photinos, which are lighter than the visible sector SUSY breaking scale, mix significantly with the bino and hence couple to the Standard Model sufficiently strongly to leave potentially observable traces. In particular, volume modulus and inflaton decays generically induce a cosmological abundance of dark photinos that can explain dark matter. We find that the `natural Photinoverse dark matter parameter space' is already accessible to current experiments, notably gamma ray observations, which therefore have discovery potential in the near future.
papers.reason: Explores dark photinos from string compactifications mixing with the bino as a dark matter candidate, relevant for portal searches.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for quark Dyson--Schwinger equations and propagator singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) framework for solving the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson--Schwinger equation at real and complex momenta. The resulting dressing functions agree closely with conventional iterative solutions. We investigate the singularity structure of the quark propagator using two complementary methods. Analytic continuation of a PINN trained on the real momentum axis estimates the locations of poles and further reveals three complex-conjugate pole pairs. An independent reconstruction using PINN-parametrized spectral densities and a single pole pair yields $q=-0.146\pm0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. The agreement between the two methods substantially strengthens confidence in the properties of the leading singularities. Both spectral densities change sign, and the negative regions of the vector density and the complex poles indicate a violation of reflection positivity, consistent with quark confinement. Finally, we use the extracted poles and residues to calculate their contributions to two order parameters at finite quark chemical potential, the chiral condensate and the quark number density.
papers.reason: Applies physics-informed neural networks to solve quark Dyson-Schwinger equations and analyze propagator singularities and confinement.

papers.title: Introducing Parton-Level Fluctuations in the TRENTo-Sea Model
papers.abstract: A variety of experimental and theoretical data suggest that initial condition models for heavy-ion collisions contain a degree of sub-nucleonic fluctuations. While current models fit the number and size of these fluctuations to data, we use nuclear parton distribution functions to constrain sub-nucleonic structure and fluctuations in TRENTo-Sea, an extension of TRENTo. Sampling the momentum fraction distributions of quarks and gluons in heavy ions, we use perturbative quantum chromodynamics to collide nuclei at the parton level, and we introduce an infrared center-of-momentum damping scale which is tuned to proton-proton cross sections. We find that our model successfully reproduces the $\varepsilon_2\{2\}$ of data-calibrated models except in central collisions, and an analysis of the power spectrum and granularity of the pre-equilibrium fireball shows that the number of low-$x$ partons in a nucleon has a significant effect on the local transverse geometry. Our model is largely insensitive to variations of the infrared parameters, as such changes are absorbed into the calibration of the infrared regulator. We expect that this work will aid future research on soft-hard correlations and constraining different nPDF sets.
papers.reason: Introduces sub-nucleonic parton-level fluctuations into the TRENTo-Sea heavy-ion model using nuclear PDFs and perturbative QCD.

papers.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
papers.abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.
papers.reason: Constructs a coherent quantum circuit simulation for Mueller dipole branching at small $x$, relevant for DIS phenomenology.

papers.title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
papers.abstract: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K e\nu_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.
papers.topic: Kaon DAs and D->K form factor
papers.reason: Fits the $D\to K$ transition form factor using BESIII data and LCSRs to determine kaon distribution amplitudes and extract $|V_{cs}|$, bridging flavor physics and QCD inputs.

papers.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
papers.abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.
papers.reason: Uses supermassive black hole accretion flows as a bolometer to constrain sub-MeV dark matter-electron scattering.

papers.title: Continuous Universal Fake Factors for jet-to-tau background estimation
papers.abstract: We study Continuous Universal Fake Factors (CUFF), a method for estimating backgrounds from jets misidentified as hadronic tau candidates. CUFF combines four reference-region fake factors for each target tau candidate failing Loose identification. Their weights depend on candidate features and target fail-Loose distributions after subtracting simulated contributions from genuine taus and electrons or muons misidentified as tau candidates. We use ATLAS 2015-2016 Open Data with tau candidates matched to jets with $20<p_T^{\rm jet}\leq60$ GeV. In eight mixtures of reference samples with known proportions, predicted total yields for the Medium identification selection differ from data after subtraction by $+0.7\%$ to $+4.3\%$, supporting the combination. In two validation regions, the corresponding differences are $-21.85\%$ and $-45.84\%$, with statistical uncertainties, including training fluctuations, of $1.58\%$ and $6.03\%$ relative to the data references. These discrepancies lie within broad empirical uncertainty ranges from simulation comparisons between regions, widened by limited simulation statistics. For Loose identification, CUFF and the Universal Fake Factor (UFF) method adapted to public data give similar inclusive yields in one validation region, while CUFF agrees more closely with the data reference in the other. CUFF also describes the shapes of several kinematic distributions more accurately than adapted UFF, including that of an observable not used as a model input. Across nine identification thresholds, relative yield differences vary gradually from $-26.4\%$ to $-19.7\%$ and $-50.2\%$ to $-40.6\%$ in the two regions, respectively, demonstrating consistent application of CUFF at continuously variable tau-identification thresholds without retraining.
papers.topic: Continuous Universal Fake Factors for tau ID
papers.reason: Discusses background estimation methods for jet-to-tau misidentification at colliders, relevant to experimental systematic techniques.

papers.title: Ratio of $\bar{\Lambda}$ to $K_\rm{S}^0$ production cross-sections in $pp$ collisions at 13.6TeV
papers.abstract: The production cross-section ratio of promptly produced $\bar{\Lambda}$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ hadrons is measured in proton-proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6TeV recorded in 2024 with the upgraded LHCb detector and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $64\rm{pb}^{-1}$. The ratio is presented as a function of transverse momentum, $p_\rm{T}$, and rapidity, $y$, in the ranges $0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\rm{GeV}/c$ and $2.0 < y < 4.5$. The results are in good agreement with previous measurements at different centre-of-mass energies. They are compared to predictions from currently available event generators and can be used as input in future event generator tunings.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
papers.reason: Measures prompt $\bar{\Lambda}$ to $K_S^0$ production cross-section ratios in pp collisions at 13.6 TeV at LHCb. [favorite author: Jordy de Vries]

papers.title: Entanglement entropy in low x Deep Inelastic Scattering
papers.abstract: In a 2017 paper by Kharzeev and Levin, it has been proposed that hadronic entropy, extracted from the multiplicity of final state hadrons, provides a measure of entanglement in the proton wave function, observed in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) of electrons and protons. In this contribution we discuss how the density matrix of the low x DIS system can give rise to a mixed state and therefore to finite entanglement entropy. We further present recent numerical results on the determination of low x dipole multiplicities, based on the solution of the Levin-Lublinsky evolution equation.
papers.reason: Touches upon entanglement in DIS, adjacent to partonic structure relevant to deep-inelastic neutrino scattering.

papers.title: CLEAR: A Contrastive-Masked Foundation Model for BESIII Event Understanding
papers.abstract: The increasing diversity and complexity of decay channels at high energy physics experiments pose a challenge to analysis workflows, which require time-consuming, labor-intensive channel-specific selections and optimization. This motivates the development of foundation models capable of learning a unified representation transferable across different channels. In this paper, we introduce CLEAR (Contrastive Learning for Event Attention-based Representation), a foundation model designed for physics analysis at BESIII that combines masked modeling and contrastive learning to support decay channel classification and anomaly detection. Masked modeling trains the encoder to predict masked particle features by learning inter-particle correlations, while contrastive learning improves the local clusterability and linear separability of the representation space for discrimination. By further examining the balance between alignment and uniformity, we investigate how contrastive learning shapes the local neighborhood geometry of the representation space and how this geometry relates to classification and anomaly detection performance. Decay channel classification favors a balance between alignment and uniformity, whereas anomaly detection benefits from a greater relative weight on uniformity. For exclusive final-state identification, CLEAR achieves higher signal efficiency than conventional cut-based methods at matched purity and provides a framework that can potentially be extended to other high-energy physics experiments.
papers.topic: Foundation model for BESIII event understanding
papers.reason: Applies contrastive learning and masked modeling for event representation at BESIII, touching upon ML workflows for high energy physics.

papers.title: Testing the Unitarity of Three-Flavor Neutrino Mixing above the GUT Scale
papers.abstract: We investigate how physics between the grand-unification and Planck scales affects neutrino mixing in the standard three-flavor framework, distinguishing genuine non unitarity from unitary shifts of the mixing parameters. First, we show that heavy gauge singlet states at or above the grand-unification scale induce deviations from unitarity of the effective (3\times3) Pontecorvo Maki Nakagawa Sakata (PMNS) matrix, suppressed by the ratio of the light-neutrino mass to the heavy mass. The resulting effects are estimated to be of order (10^{-27}), far below current oscillation constraints. Second, we examine the impact of a flavor-blind dimension-five Weinberg operator suppressed by a high-energy scale (\Lambda). This operator modifies the neutrino mass matrix and shifts the mixing angles while preserving the exact unitarity of the PMNS matrix. Using the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit parameters for normal mass ordering, including the Dirac CP-violating phase, and numerically diagonalizing the corrected complex-symmetric mass matrix, we find that the shift in (\theta_{12}) can reach approximately (0.12^\circ) at the Planck scale for a quasi-degenerate neutrino spectrum, compared with (0.011^\circ) for normal ordering. The corrections increase as (1/\Lambda), reaching approximately (6.5^\circ) for normal ordering near the grand-unification scale, where perturbation theory becomes unreliable for the quasi-degenerate spectrum. Since the Weinberg operator acts entirely within the active three-flavor sector, it introduces no additional non-unitarity parameters; instead, the correlated shifts of the three mixing angles are governed by a single parameter. Our results demonstrate that tests of active-flavor probability conservation cannot directly constrain this high-scale contribution. Its phenomenological signatures must instead be sought in the correlated modifications of the neutrino mixing parameters.
papers.reason: Examines non-unitarity and Weinberg operator shifts of the PMNS matrix above the GUT scale, but effects on low-energy oscillations are extremely small.

papers.title: Anatomy of charge radii of Ca nuclei in self-consistent approaches with Skyrme and Fayans functionals
papers.abstract: It has been known that the $^{40-48}$Ca nuclei have anomalous $N$-dependence of their charge radii. While difficult to reproduce in most self-consistent calculations, the parabolic behavior in $^{42,44,46}$Ca is reproduced with the Fayans functional, although it tends to overestimate the charge radii at the neutron-deficient $^{38}$Ca. We investigate the origin of the $N$-dependence with the Fayans functional by decomposing it into radial contributions, and trace it back to the single-particle potentials and neutron pair densities. The results are compared with those of a Skyrme functional SkM$^\ast$, which is considered a representative of the usual functionals. It is found that, in the results of the Fayans functional, the origin is shared between the parabolic behavior in $^{42,44,46}$Ca and the erroneous enhancement of the charge radii at $^{38}$Ca.
